**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 2 (0730), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Paper 2: Section A - Summary and Text Reconstruction; Section B - Composition; Section C - Prescribed Texts. Duration: three hours.**

Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty.

In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will be penalised.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

A pre-prepared or memorised composition will be severely sanctioned.

incertitudes: Texte a trous : le sujet imprime « QUESTIONS 2 » (pluriel) et « Overtime » (en un mot), « 170.000 cases » et « 65.000 deaths » avec un point comme separateur de milliers ; tout est recopie tel quel. Les 15 blancs sont numerotes (1) a (15) comme imprime.

Le blanc (6) est suivi de « a » sur la meme ligne du sujet (« the Government (6) ____ a prevention and response plan ») : la reponse modele est « put in place » ; plusieurs reponses sont possibles pour chaque blanc, le corrige en donne une et des variantes dans la colonne Rule.
Le bareme du sujet n'indique que 15 points pour la question ; un point par blanc est une hypothese de correction, pas un bareme imprime.

**QUESTIONS 2: TEXT RECONSTRUCTION (15 marks)**

*Read the following text and fill the blanks using suitable words of your choice.*

*Ladies and Gentlemen,*

In December 2019, the coronavirus outbreak was (1) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ in the Wuhan Province of the People's Republic of China. Overtime, it gradually (2) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ to Asia, Europe and Africa, resulting (3) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ the quarantine and death of several people. A few days later, the World Health Organization (4) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ that the coronavirus has gone from an epidemic to a pandemic, with over 170.000 cases in 146 countries, and about 65.000 deaths. Cameroon, like many states in the world, is not (5) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ from this pandemic. From the very first hours of its emergence, the Government (6) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ a prevention and response plan aimed at (7) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ the spread of this pandemic. To date, people have been diagnosed (8) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ this virus in our country and are being (9) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ by specialized services. It should be noted, however, that so far, no local outbreaks of this (10) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ have been (11) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ in Cameroon and the cases (12) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ so far are persons who have recently been abroad or persons who have come in contact with them. However, in the face of what now appears to be a global health (13) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_, the (14) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ taken so far deserve to be strengthened (15) \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ prevent the spread of this virus in our country.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reconstructed text** (one possible answer for each blank; the paper accepts any word or phrase of your choice that fits the grammar and the sense)

*Ladies and Gentlemen,*

In December 2019, the coronavirus outbreak was **detected** in the Wuhan Province of the People's Republic of China. Overtime, it gradually **spread** to Asia, Europe and Africa, resulting **in** the quarantine and death of several people. A few days later, the World Health Organization **declared** that the coronavirus has gone from an epidemic to a pandemic, with over 170.000 cases in 146 countries, and about 65.000 deaths. Cameroon, like many states in the world, is not **spared** from this pandemic. From the very first hours of its emergence, the Government **put in place** a prevention and response plan aimed at **curbing** the spread of this pandemic. To date, people have been diagnosed **with** this virus in our country and are being **treated** by specialized services. It should be noted, however, that so far, no local outbreaks of this **disease** have been **recorded** in Cameroon and the cases **confirmed** so far are persons who have recently been abroad or persons who have come in contact with them. However, in the face of what now appears to be a global health **emergency**, the **measures** taken so far deserve to be strengthened **in order to** prevent the spread of this virus in our country.

**Before / after / rule**

| Blank | Answer | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| (1) | detected | was + past participle (passive, past); a verb of discovery. Also: reported, identified, first recorded. |
| (2) | spread | past simple of the irregular verb spread, spread, spread, after the adverb "gradually". |
| (3) | in | "result in" + noun introduces the effect; "result from" introduces the cause. |
| (4) | declared | reporting verb + that-clause, past simple in the sequence "A few days later". Also: announced, confirmed. |
| (5) | spared | "be spared from" (or "immune from", "exempt from"): a participle or adjective that takes "from". |
| (6) | put in place | verb phrase whose object is "a prevention and response plan" (the printed "a" follows the blank). Also: drew up, set up, adopted. |
| (7) | curbing | -ing form after the preposition "at" (aimed at ...); meaning: reducing or stopping. Also: stopping, containing, halting. |
| (8) | with | "be diagnosed with" + illness. |
| (9) | treated | present passive progressive "are being + past participle". Also: managed, cared for. |
| (10) | disease | noun after the demonstrative "this"; collocation "outbreak of a disease". Also: virus, pandemic, illness. |
| (11) | recorded | present perfect passive "have been + past participle". Also: reported, registered, detected. |
| (12) | confirmed | past participle as a reduced relative clause ("the cases which have been confirmed"). Also: diagnosed, recorded, reported. |
| (13) | emergency | collocation "global health emergency". Also: crisis, threat. |
| (14) | measures | plural noun, subject of "deserve"; "measures taken". Also: steps, actions, precautions. |
| (15) | in order to | expression of purpose + base verb "prevent". Also: so as to, to. |

**Marking grid (15 marks).** There are 15 blanks for 15 marks, so each correct blank is worth one mark (the scheme itself is not printed). A word earns the mark when it is grammatically correct in its place (tense, form, preposition, number), fits the meaning, and is spelt correctly.

**Common mistakes**

1. A word that fits the sense but not the grammar: "spreaded", "resulting to", "diagnosed of", "are being treat".
2. Filling a blank without reading the words that follow it: for blank (6) the printed "a" requires a verb phrase that takes a singular object ("put in place a plan"), and blank (15) must lead to the base form "prevent".
3. Repeating the same word in neighbouring blanks (recorded, recorded) instead of varying the vocabulary (recorded, confirmed).
